samples.summary: Format-painter pick-up behaviour changed on the keyboard path, against the issue's "keyboard shortcuts behave exactly as before" criterion and its "pure wiring: no new document behaviour" framing
samples.evidence: `copyFormat()` no longer reads the caret: it calls `formatSourcePosition()`, which for any non-empty selection reads `normalized.start.offset + 1` instead of `this.cursor.position`, and `captureFormatAtCursor` now destructures away `image`, `pageNumber` and `href`. Both are reached by the existing `Mod+Shift+C` handler (text-editor.ts:1093), so a shipped keyboard flow now picks up a different style object than before. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:3-5, 34, 57) states the task is pure wiring and that "the shortcuts must keep behaving exactly as they do now". The changes look like improvements, but they are behaviour changes the issue explicitly excluded, and the todo's own follow-up section names them without amending the criterion.

samples.summary: New general URL-safety primitives added inside the docs Markdown serializer rather than `@wafflebase/core/url`, the repo's documented home for them — sibling emitters now answer "is this URL safe to emit?" differently
samples.evidence: `UNEMITTABLE_URL_CHARS`, `isEmittableUrl` and `SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI` are module-private to packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts. docs/design/frontend.md:466-470 and docs/design/cli.md:1711-1714 state that `@wafflebase/core/url` is "the package's existing home for URL-safety primitives that had already been duplicated once" and that a partially applied guard "is worse than none, because it reads as covered". packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:834 and packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1662,2004 still gate on bare `isSafeUrl`, and the `data:image/...` allowlist (which the PDF/image paths also need a rule for) exists only here. The Markdown-destination-termination part is genuinely serializer-specific, but the C0/C1-control and `data:image` allowlist parts are not.

samples.summary: Dialog hardcodes inches and its own `PX_PER_INCH`, while the docs ruler beside it already ships locale-aware unit selection — a metric user sees cm on the ruler and inches in the dialog
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/ruler/unit.ts exports `detectUnit(locale)` (returns 'cm' outside inch locales) and `getGridConfig(unit, pxPerInch = 96)`, used by the docs ruler that edits the very same margins. The dialog re-declares `const PX_PER_INCH = 96` and labels every field "(inches)" unconditionally. The issue's non-goals exclude "a cm/mm unit toggle", not locale-derived units, so reuse of the shipped helper was available and would have kept the two margin surfaces consistent.

samples.summary: The new frontend Markdown / plain-text export surface is recorded only as a roadmap table tick; no canonical subsystem design doc mentions it, unlike page setup which got a docs-pagination.md section
searchedFor: glob docs/design/**/import-export*.md (none; only packages/documentation/guide/import-export.md, a user guide)
read docs/design/export-progress.md §C which enumerates the docs export button and its onProgress wiring
read docs/design/docs/docs-pdf-export.md:391 ("the export menu … becomes a dropdown")
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs-wordprocessor-roadmap.md:71 adds `| Markdown / plain-text export | ✅ |` and the audit paragraph mentions it, but no subsystem doc describes the new `text-actions.ts` module, its `inlineImages: true` divergence from the CLI default, or the fact that these two entries thread no `onProgress` — while docs/design/export-progress.md:108 is the doc that documents exactly that wiring for the docs export button and is untouched. Page setup, by contrast, was correctly folded into docs-pagination.md.

samples.summary: `FormatPainterToggle` re-implements the shape of the shipped slides `FormatPainterButton` in app-local code rather than in the shared `components/text-formatting/` folder the two toolbars otherwise share
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/format-painter.tsx is the same Toggle + IconBrush + `useEffect` subscribe-to-editor pattern (`isPaintingFormat`/`onPaintFormatChange` vs `hasCopiedFormat`/`onCopiedFormatChange`). The repo already factors cross-editor toolbar controls into packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/ (e.g. clear-formatting-button.tsx, insert-link-button.tsx). The semantics genuinely differ (docs has no pointer paint mode — an explicit non-goal in the task), so this is a preference, not a requirement.

samples.summary: `setPageSetup` throws a `RangeError` where every other mutating `EditorAPI` member is total (no-ops or returns a boolean), and in read-only mode the same call silently no-ops instead of throwing
samples.evidence: `assertUsablePageSetup` throws from `writePageSetup`, which is also the ruler's `onMarginChange` path, while the `MUTATING_METHODS` allowlist replaces `setPageSetup` with a bare no-op in read-only — so the documented contract (docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md "throws a RangeError") holds only when the editor is writable. The validation itself is well-motivated; the inconsistency of the API shape is the point.
